To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the financial cycle is an appropriate early warning system for recessions and that the financial cycle component related to the global financial cycle seems to be the best predictor of recessions.

the financial cycle is an appropriate indicator for predicting economic recessions and, in this respect, the financial cycle related to global financial market participants’ risk aversion is a particularly good predictor of future economic recessions.

the synthetic financial cycle measures based on the dynamic factor model have predictive power for the prediction and forecasting of economic recessions and that the factor related to global financial conditions seems to be the most important indicator for policymakers.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and application of dynamic factor models in order to construct synthetic financial cycle components for the analysis of the interaction between the financial and real economy.
the construction and analysis of a large set of financial cycle measures that may be used for the analysis and prediction of economic activity and inflation.
the development of new tools that could help to better understand and forecast the financial cycle, which is a key element for the design of appropriate monetary and macroprudential policies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed financial cycle measures are a valuable tool for the design of monetary and macroprudential policies.
the financial cycle is not a homogeneous concept, but rather consists of several different subcomponents.
the synthetic financial cycle measures constructed in this paper have significant predictive power and can be used to complement existing recession forecasting models.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
financial cycles are important drivers of the business cycle.

a financial cycle measure based on a large set of macroeconomic variables has a significant predictive power for recessions, and thus could be an appropriate early warning tool for macroprudential policymakers.
the financial cycle measures proposed in this paper are useful for macroprudential analysis and the design of monetary and macroprudential policies.
The main takeaway from our work is that

a large set of financial variables can be reduced to three synthetic factors that are able to explain a substantial amount of variation in the macroeconomic data and have predictive power for economic downturns.
the analysis of the financial system as a whole is crucial for the design of an effective macroprudential framework and for the conduct of macroeconomic policy.
financial cycle measures based on a large number of financial variables can be constructed using dynamic factor models and that these measures have significant forecasting power.
